title: Avalanche (AVAX) Price Prediction: Can AVAX Reach $15 After Its Latest Breakout?
summary: AVAX price is approaching a critical stage as a trendline breakout, renewed ETF inflows, and growing adoption put the $15 target into focus.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: AVAX

AVAX price is approaching a critical stage as a trendline breakout, renewed ETF inflows, and growing adoption put the $15 target into focus.

After briefly reaching $7.61, AVAX’s current price has pulled back towards $7.33, bringing the recent trendline breakout under its first real test. Traders are now watching whether buyers can defend the $7.20 support and push the price back towards the key $7.80–$8.00 resistance zone.

AVAX Breaks Above Short-Term Descending Trendline

AVAX price has triggered a short-term breakout after spending several sessions beneath a descending trendline. The move developed after AVAX established a local base around $7.25-$7.40 and began pushing back towards $7.60.

Trader Symba highlighted the breakout as AVAX moved through the trendline near $7.60. The structure is notable because the descending resistance had controlled price since the earlier move above $8, making the latest break the first meaningful attempt to shift short-term momentum.

AVAX price has since retraced towards $7.33, meaning the next test is whether buyers can defend the breakout structure rather than allowing price to fall straight back below the former trendline. A recovery towards $7.60-$7.70 would strengthen the move, while continued weakness towards the recent lows would make the breakout less convincing.

Avalanche triggered a breakout through its short-term descending trendline after forming a local base near the recent lows. Source: Trader Symba via X

AVAX ETF Marks Inflows Return

Institutional demand has also started showing signs of improvement. Recent data shows approximately $1.57 million in daily net inflows into AVAX spot ETFs, marking a return of positive flows after a quieter period.

AVAX spot ETFs recorded roughly $1.57 million in daily net inflows. Source: JP Futures via X

The ETF products now hold approximately $40.27 million in total net assets, while the latest displayed trading value stands near $155,800. AVAX was trading around $7.60 when the latest flow data was recorded. The inflow remains relatively modest compared with larger crypto ETF markets, but the return to positive flows is still constructive. Continued inflows would suggest that demand is beginning to rebuild alongside the improving technical setup.

AVAX and Its Increasing Global Adoption

Avalanche is beginning to gain more attention for real-world use cases beyond crypto trading. One of the latest additions is the reported integration of Avalanche with UAE PASS, the United Arab Emirates’ national digital identity system.

UAE PASS serves more than 11 million users, meaning the integration could place Avalanche technology inside a much larger digital services ecosystem. This would give the network exposure to government-backed identity infrastructure and potentially expand how Avalanche is used across real-world applications.

The development adds to the broader adoption narrative around AVAX. Rather than relying only on DeFi or speculative activity, integrations tied to digital identity and public infrastructure could give Avalanche more practical use cases and strengthen its position as a blockchain built for wider institutional and government adoption.

Higher-Timeframe AVAX Setup Targets $15.17

The larger AVAX price is beginning to show a more ambitious recovery setup after months of persistent downside. Price has spent several weeks forming a base around the $6-$8 region while gradually moving away from the lower boundary of a descending structure.

A higher-timeframe AVAX setup projects a larger recovery towards approximately $15.17. Source: Sheldon Diedericks via X

Crypto analyst Sheldon Diedericks’ chart shows AVAX attempting to break from this long-term decline, with the next major target positioned around $15.17. Reaching that area would require AVAX price to first overcome the resistance sitting immediately above the current market, including the broader $8-$10 region. The chart also shows an important moving average near $8, meaning that area remains one of the first technical hurdles before the larger $15 target can become more realistic. Holding the current base and establishing higher lows would strengthen the recovery scenario.

$7.20 Level Remains Important AVAX Support

The latest pullback means AVAX price is now testing whether the recent improvement can survive a retest. Brave New Coin data places the latest 24-hour low around $7.20, making this the immediate level to watch beneath the current $7.33 price.

Holding above $7.20 would preserve the recent base and leave room for another attempt towards $7.60. Beyond that, AVAX Avalanche would need to recover the $7.80-$8.00 area before the short-term structure becomes significantly stronger.

AVAX is trading near $7.33, down 2.66% over the last 24 hours. Source: Brave New Coin

A decisive loss of $7.20 would weaken the breakout and could return attention towards the broader $7.00 region, followed by the previous base closer to $6 if selling pressure expands. The upside case therefore depends less on the initial breakout itself and more on whether AVAX price can now defend the higher structure that followed it.

Looking Ahead: AVAX Bullish Triggers?

AVAX price is entering an important phase where improving technicals are beginning to overlap with stronger fundamental narratives. The short-term trendline breakout, renewed ETF inflows, and growing real-world adoption through developments such as UAE PASS are giving the recovery a stronger backdrop than price action alone.

The next step is confirmation. AVAX needs to protect its recent base while gradually clearing the resistance sitting overhead. The main bullish triggers to watch are:

  • Hold $7.20: Keeps the recent base and breakout structure intact.
  • Reclaim $7.60: Would show buyers are regaining short-term momentum.
  • Break $7.80-$8.00: This remains the bigger confirmation zone and could strengthen the case for a wider recovery.
  • Move towards $10: A sustained breakout above $8 would begin putting the psychological $10 level back into focus.
  • Higher-timeframe target near $15.17: This becomes considerably more relevant if AVAX can establish a sustained trend above the $8-$10 region.
  • ETF inflows and adoption remain supportive: Continued institutional demand and expanding real-world use cases would add fundamental support to the technical recovery.

A fall back below $7.20 would weaken the immediate setup and could delay the recovery. For now, AVAX price is showing improving conditions, but the strongest bullish confirmation would come from turning the $7.80-$8.00 region from resistance into support.

title: Treasury Sanctions Iranian Crypto Exchange BitBank Over Bitcoin Transfers to IRGC
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Treasury Sanctions Iranian Crypto Exchange BitBank Over Bitcoin Transfers to IRGC
The U.S. is targeting Iran's use of crypto — specifically bitcoin. 
This post Treasury Sanctions Iranian Crypto Exchange BitBank Over Bitcoin Transfers to IRGC first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and i...
content:
The U.S. is continuing to target Iran’s use of bitcoin. 

In a Thursday statement, the U.S. Department of the Treasury designated BitBank, an Iranian crypto exchange, as part of Operation Economic Outcast — the Trump Administration’s whole-of-government economic campaign against the Islamic Republic of Iran and its enablers. 

The U.S. has sanctioned Iran for decades. This year, the Middle Eastern country has stepped up its use of cryptocurrencies — including bitcoin — in order to skirt around economic penalties. 

“Today’s designations of Iranian digital asset infrastructure make perfectly clear that efforts to finance the Iranian regime using cryptocurrencies are not beyond OFAC’s reach,” Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent said in a statement. 

“If you support the Iranian regime, the Department of the Treasury will sanction you.”

The sanctions target designated Iranian financier Babak Zanjani, along with its software developer, Pishtaz Simorgh Electronic Trade Company, and three of Zanjani’s associates: Hossein Ali Zaker Hossein, Mohammad Mahdi Zaker Hossein, and Seyed Adel Heidari.

Since June, the Iranian Hormuz Safe Marine Services Authority has used BitBank to move bitcoin to the Iranian regime, according to the Treasury. 

Thursday’s sanctions aim to hit the “architecture Zanjani built to launder funds,” it added. 

“The Department of the Treasury will continue to not only target the Iranian digital asset ecosystem, but also international entities and actors which help facilitate it,” the statement continued. 

Iran started a bitcoin-backed insurance service for its counties shipping companies earlier this year.

The U.S. in July said that it had frozen crypto linked to the Iranian regime, mostly in the form of Tether’s stablecoin. 

Stablecoins like Tether’s USDT can be frozen by the company that issues the asset. But bitcoin, being decentralized and having no single issuer, cannot. 

The U.S. Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control in July said Iran had been dodging sanctions by accepting pay in bitcoin from ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz. 

OFAC said at the time that Hormuz Safe, developed by Iran’s Ministry of Economy, “accepts payment in Bitcoin and other digital assets” so it can bypass sanctions. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Bitcoin Price Unlikely To Be Bothered by Interest Rate Hike: Grayscale
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Unlikely To Be Bothered by Interest Rate Hike: Grayscale
The Federal Reserve hiked interest rates on Wednesday — and may do so again this year — but bitcoin's price is unlikely to be hurt, Grayscale argued. 
This post Bitcoin Price Unlikely To Be Bothered by Interest ...
content:
The Federal Reserve hiked interest rates for the first time since 2023 on Wednesday and it sent the bitcoin price — briefly — all over the place. 

But then it settled and currently sits a modest 1% higher over a 24-hour period. 

And according to asset manager Grayscale’s crypto research team, bitcoin is unlikely to be bothered by the Fed’s decision. 

“We believe yesterday’s move was a mid-cycle adjustment, not a cyclical change,” wrote the firm’s head of research, Zach Pandl, in a Thursday note. 

“And we doubt the one or two rate hikes expected for 2026 will lead to much change in capital allocation.”

Bitcoin has — in the past but not always — done well in a low interest rate environment. And when the Federal Reserve has in the past increased borrowing costs, the price of the leading digital asset has slid. 

That’s because low interest rates means more liquidity for investors to take risks and buy assets like bitcoin. 

Pandl added that when the Fed in 2022 started ramping up interest rates to contain inflation, it “probably weighed on the price of bitcoin” because it “meaningfully affected the opportunity cost of holding non-interest-bearing assets.” 

But this time feels more like 1997, argued Pandl, when the Federal Reserve did a one off hike and the Nasdaq kept moving higher.

Bitcoin’s price recently stood at close to $76,581, up 18% over the past 30 days. The coin  in August benefited from news that the U.S. Treasury would at least double the size of its liquidity-support buyback operations.

The U.S. is currently in the grips of an affordability crisis and inflation is hurting households as oil prices surge. 

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said the central bank was focused on bringing down inflation. 

“The plain fact is that inflation is too high, and has been for too long,” he said on Wednesday. 

U.S. President Donald Trump has repeatedly said that he wants interest rates to be lower. Writing on his Truth Social platform on Wednesday, he said: “Interest Rates in the United States should be 1%, or less, because we are the Best Credit in the World — BY FAR.”

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: SEC Clears Path for Tokenized Stocks With 5-Year Onchain Trading Exemption
summary:
Key Takeaways: The SEC has introduced a five-year “Innovation Exemption” to permit trading of U.S. stocks by tokenizing them on approved venues. With a permissioned AMM liquidity pool, Tokenized Securities
The post SEC Clears Path for Tokenized Stocks With 5-Year Onchain Trading Exemption appeared f...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The SEC has introduced a five-year “Innovation Exemption” to permit trading of U.S. stocks by tokenizing them on approved venues.
  • With a permissioned AMM liquidity pool, Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs) can comply with investor protection’s necessary rules.
  • With onchain securities trading, the agency is looking to receive public input on considered permanent rules.

The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has unveiled a new regulatory framework that could accelerate the adoption of tokenized stocks in the United States.

On September 17, the agency announced a temporary “Innovation Exemption” that grants conditional relief to Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs), allowing them to facilitate trading of tokenized National Market System (NMS) stocks through blockchain-based infrastructure.

  • SEC Opens Door to Onchain Stock Trading
  • Key Rules for Tokenized Securities Venues
    • Compliance Requirements
    • Liquidity Providers Also Receive Relief

SEC Opens Door to Onchain Stock Trading

Property tax exemption is granted for the operation of TSV as a “not a traditional exchange” under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.

Permissioned automated market makers (AMMs) and liquidity pools can facilitate the assembly of sellers and buyers for tokenized stocks in these venues. The framework is aimed at providing protections for investors and the marketplace, while encouraging innovation,” the SEC said.

SEC Commissioner Paul Atkins called it a vital step forward in modernizing U.S. capital markets and allowing regulated onchain trading for some equity securities. The exemption is temporary and runs for five years from the date of publication, unless the exemptions are to be revoked by further regulation.

Read More: SEC Eyes Tokenized Stocks Plan That Could Unlock Trillions in Crypto Trading Markets

Key Rules for Tokenized Securities Venues

The SEC placed several conditions on the relief. TSVs must ensure that tokenized shares have the same rights and privileges as the underlying shares. Capitals on number of symbols listed, and trading volume, also for platforms.

Compliance Requirements

TVS must meet several critical requirements under the order. To support tokenized stock trading, smart contracts should be open, verifiable and built on a public permissionless chain.

If the underlying stock is suspended from the main exchange, trading of tokenized shares should be suspended. Platforms must also make public information on their trading activities and operations. Further, before an unaffiliated third party tokenizes a company’s shares, the issuer would have to be alerted and provided an opportunity to object.

While the SEC noted that the measures are geared toward safeguarding investors, they also enable experimentation with possible blockchain-based structures of markets.

Liquidity Providers Also Receive Relief

Additionally, the order provides conditional exemption from issuance of “dealer” registration for liquidity providers in TSV-registered liquidity pools.

This applies to the participants who offer liquidity through their own capital and could add to what is described as typical market-making activity. Expect the exemption to have a positive impact on liquidity for token-based stock trading venues during the pilot.

The SEC is seeking public comment on any aspects of the framework, such as proposed amendments and further action.

The announcement is one of an unmistakable move by regulators in the U.S. to expand blockchain-based security markets. The framework is a temporary solution, but it does offer a clear process for trading tokenized securities as traditional financial assets advance onto blockchain networks.

content:
Key Takeaways:

  • COTI has already ported Privacy-on-Demand to Avalanche, enabling private computation for C-Chain apps and Avalanche L1s.
  • The Privacy Portal is updated to include one-click AVAX and USDC on Avalanche without user transition.
  • COTI states its Garbled Circuits technology can be up to 3,000x faster and 250x smaller than other privacy solutions.

COTI has expanded its privacy infrastructure to Avalanche, giving crypto users and developers a way to handle sensitive transactions without moving assets to a separate privacy network.

The launch puts Privacy-on-Demand directly on Avalanche while adding a simple Privacy Portal for private AVAX and USDC.

https://t.co/sRlEB2E7AY

— COTI Foundation (@COTInetwork) September 16, 2026

  • COTI Brings Private Computation to Avalanche
  • Garbled Circuits Power the Privacy Layer
    • Private AVAX and USDC Arrive on C-Chain
    • Privacy Targets Avalanche’s Growing Crypto Economy

COTI Brings Private Computation to Avalanche

Privacy-on-Demand is designed to work on top of existing Avalanche applications, tokens, and smart contracts. Developers do not need to move their assets to a dedicated privacy chain to use COTI’s infrastructure.

The system handles sensitive data in a private way and provides an encrypted answer. With this, transactions will retain their data and business logic without revealing the underlying assets’ details to the applications.

The infrastructure can enable multiple use cases for crypto, such as private stablecoin transfers, confidential payments, private DeFi, tokenized assets and more that demand selective data disclosure, COTI reminds.

The same measurement also works for Avalanche L1s. Projects can incorporate privacy options without constructing a new infrastructure with a separate network.

Read More: Avalanche Targets Japan’s $1.6T Bond Market With Progmat Collaboration

Garbled Circuits Power the Privacy Layer

The technology behind COTI is based on multi-party computation known as Garbled Circuits, which enables a calculation to be performed without revealing the actual data.

COTI also says that it runs up to 3,000 times faster and 250 times less weight than other privacy technologies, although it compared them based on its own advantages.

Private AVAX and USDC Arrive on C-Chain

This launch also sees the introduction of COTI’s Privacy Portal to Avalanche C-Chain. The portal enables users to make tokens private in a fairly straight-forward way. Private balances exist at launch, and at any point in time a user can opt to send/receive and hold AVAX and USDC while keeping their private balance data only visible to them.

Users can also take assets back down to the public side if necessary. That allows Avalanche users to test out and practice confidential transactions without leaving the platform. With regard to stablecoins, the attribute may enable payment, settlement, and other scenarios that require private disclosure of balances or settlement amounts being made.

Privacy Targets Avalanche’s Growing Crypto Economy

COTI is preparing the infrastructure for more than private transfers of tokens. The company cites opportunities in tokenization of real world assets, stablecoins, payments, payroll, private DeFi, and Avalanche L1s. Private computation may also be used, to provide a limited amount of public data with custom business logic by the developer.

Selective disclosure is another part of the design. The necessary data can be made available to authorized parties when required for compliance or verification, whilst still leaving other data private by default.

Now Privacy-on-Demand is available on Avalanche, COTI is taking its privacy technology to the next level by allowing it to be integrated into infrastructure alongside existing crypto applications and assets.

title: Vitalik Says AI Can Secure Crypto, Keeps 90% of His Wealth in Crypto Despite AI Hacks
summary:

The post Vitalik Says AI Can Secure Crypto, Keeps 90% of His Wealth in Crypto Despite AI Hacks appeared first ...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Vitalik Buterin claims that AI does not spell the end of cybersecurity, stating that more effective verification may benefit defenders.
  • In short, roughly 90% of his net worth is in crypto; security is a personal bet, says Buterin.
  • AI aid in formal verification is essential for the security of Ethereum, privacy technologies, and cryptography, he believes.

The worries surrounding the ability of AI to match hacking level have risen, and Vitalik Buterin, one of the founders of Ethereum has addressed the concern. He argued in a new comment that if better math checks were used then critical software could be much harder to exploit.

It’s an increasingly common take that AI hacking means cybersecurity is doomed.

I disagree. I think cybersecurity is naturally defense-favoring once people get their shit together. And anyone who continues to hold cryptocurrency (including me, ~90% of my net worth) is implicitly…

— vitalik.eth (@VitalikButerin) September 16, 2026

  • Buterin Makes a Security Bet With Crypto
  • Formal Verification Could Change Crypto Security
    • Ethereum Needs Whole-System Verification
    • AI Hackers Are Getting More Capable

Buterin Makes a Security Bet With Crypto

This is basically a bet on the security of digital systems and a wager stronger than ever against those who’ll stop at nothing to compromise it, Buterin explained. He also mentioned that about 90% of his personal wealth is in his crypto portfolio.

He’s not relying on defenders easily locating vulnerabilities sooner than hackers. Rather, he views a more gradual evolution into demonstrating that software abides by defined security rules.

The concept is particularly applicable to blockchains, where a software error can impact wallets, smart contracts, bridges, validators or full networks.

Buterin cited the work of an advanced mathematical theorem proving as what AI may yet be able to do in the future. AI tools that can be very difficult to solve mathematical problems can also be used to solve a formal security specification for a software system, he says.

Read More: Robinhood’s AI Crypto Trading Push Arrives as Robinhood Chain Tops $1B DEX Volume

Formal Verification Could Change Crypto Security

The difference, between proving defined properties and testing code, is that the latter is binary and the former isn’t. Conventional Security Testing involves audit, simulation and attack searches for bugs. Formal verification begins by stating the exact requirement that the system needs to guarantee and then performing a mathematical check to see if the system does.

Buterin pointed out that it wasn’t easy to tackle the security requirement itself. A protocol might be able to prevent unauthorized access, but not stop attacking via forgery, replay attacks, denial-of-service, or failure to a dependent aspect.

Ethereum Needs Whole-System Verification

Verifying just a few so-called critical parts might not be sufficient for crypto networks. Other supporting software, such as databases, networking layers, caches, libraries, and others, can also be included in the attack surface.

Buterin posits that the modern AI might enable quicker validation of a larger part of a full program. That could lessen the need to believe that security researchers will find all the exploitable vulnerabilities before the bad guys.

AI Hackers Are Getting More Capable

There have also been instances where Anthropic has seen the severity of AI systems gaining access to real-world thirdparty systems in the presence of security assessments. That’s what makes automated attacks and automated defences a race.

Buterin’s solution for Ethereum is not just to increase the number of AI-powered scanners. It’s writing software with precise security properties and that are more and more provable by machine.

It could shift the balance in crypto from being more one-sided, where attackers have the upper hand by relying on AI, and more toward the defenders having the edge.
